# Bundled content boundary for the public 1.0 preparation build

The baseline uses the 2014-rules System Reference Document 5.1, under
CC-BY-4.0. It does not attempt a rules-edition migration to SRD 5.2.1.
Attribution and the complete license are retained separately. Directory names
and historical `PHB`, `DMG` or `MM` identifiers are compatibility metadata, not
claims that the complete books are licensed or bundled.

## SRD-derived content

`srd-spells.json` records the 319 licensed spell subjects, source heading pages,
compatibility names and exact resource hash. Seventeen display names were
changed to their SRD names without changing their identifiers. Forty-two
non-SRD spell definitions were removed. Ten truncated descriptions were
restored from the actual SRD text; transcription errors were corrected.

The remaining catalogue contains twelve classes, their twelve SRD subclasses,
nine races, four SRD subraces, Acolyte, Grappler, 343 magic-item variants and 67
historical-pantheon deities from SRD pages 360-362. Item variants share licensed
parent rules. The removed 27 magic items and 61 Forgotten Realms/nonhuman
deities have not been silently mapped to a different item or deity. Eight magic
item display names now use their SRD names while retaining the existing IDs.

The final cleanup also removes the Human variant and six associated bonus
helpers, five unused non-SRD elf traits, the Underdark circle option, and two
non-SRD gaming-set items with their two proficiencies. Imported content can
provide definitions for these identifiers. A missing definition is reported
when a character is loaded; loading does not rewrite the existing save.

Additional class/race narrative, setting-specific subrace prose, creature lore,
expanded tool activity/DC descriptions and book marketing copy have been
removed or replaced. Tool entries use the SRD's actual tool rules. The legacy
help pages now contain original application guidance. Original name suggestions
replace the copied book name lists without changing the generator's field or
format contracts. Calculation rules for retained entries are unchanged, except
for removing the two grants to excluded gaming-set proficiencies. The spell-header comparison also corrected Wind Walk from 1 action to the SRD casting time of 1 minute, a duration-unit typo and a duplicated material-component phrase.

`srd-baseline.json` records the final resource hashes, subject identifiers,
source sections, original integration boundary and deliberate exclusions.
Changes require a fresh provenance review; an asset hash refresh alone cannot
approve new spell subjects or erase the recorded source boundary.

## Original application integration code

The starting-equipment XML is original first-party integration data: element
IDs, quantities, selection labels and coin-roll parameters. The audit of all
28 files found no descriptive text nodes, artwork or book passages. Some maps
refer to optional imported classes/backgrounds, including Artificer and 2024
content. Keeping an adapter for an identifier does not bundle the corresponding
class/background definition. The maps remain under MIT and keep imported
characters' equipment workflows available.

The same distinction applies to original ability-bonus calculations, selector
labels, source bibliography and application settings. Customization settings
and firearm-property compatibility markers now use original application help,
not copied non-SRD explanatory prose. A favored-enemy selector label is not a
bundled monster stat block or monster lore entry.

This classification of the original ID/quantity maps and functional code is
an inference from their contents and authorship, informed by the U.S. Copyright
Office's distinction between methods/systems/names and expressive text:
https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ33.pdf. It is not a general license to copy
rulebook prose, art, character descriptions or third-party databases.

## Assets and distribution scope

Legacy templates, galleries, default portrait, UI icons and backgrounds use
the maintainer-confirmed redistribution permission recorded in
`LEGACY-ASSET-PERMISSION.md`, not MIT or the SRD license. Complete templates
retain their embedded resources and existing notices. Standalone fonts have
separate license records: Open Sans (Apache-2.0/OFL-1.1) and Nodesto (CC0).
The unused unverified Zelda font is excluded from release source.

Current branding provenance is recorded in `BRANDING-PROVENANCE.md`.
User-imported content and installed character/app data are outside this
baseline migration and have not been accessed or changed. The inventory
covers the actual release resources and corresponding-source payload, not
every historical file in Git or the contents of users' imported libraries.

The corresponding-source archive excludes historical oracle binaries and the
saved-character fixtures under `Aurora.Tests/Fixtures/Characters/`, which retain
imported non-SRD descriptions. Those fixtures remain intact in the repository
for compatibility testing. They are not needed to build or relink the native
application. The source archive supplies the production source and rebuild
materials, rather than claiming distribution clearance for historical test data.

Windows x64 and Android ARM64 are the stable targets. Windows ARM64 and macOS
remain experimental, and Web remains deferred. A passing licensing gate does
not freeze, sign or publish a new application package.
